$comment: KRYLO Weekly Upstream Watch policy (docs/adr/0036-weekly-upstream-watch.md, docs/process/MULTI_HOST_CODEX_MAINTENANCE_DESIGN.md Section 15). This file stores WATCH CONFIGURATION ONLY -- which reviewed integrations to observe, how often, and which change classes matter for each. It deliberately holds no observed upstream state: `catalog/tools.json` remains the single trusted record of what KRYLO has actually reviewed, and the scheduled watch is read-only, so an unreviewed upstream ref can never become persistent trusted repository state through automation (design Section 15.3). Every entry's reviewed ref is read from tools.json at runtime via `reviewedRefSource`, never duplicated here, so the two can never disagree. Only entries whose tools.json record carries a REAL reviewed version or commit are watchable: an entry still at `pending-first-review` has no baseline to compare against and is reported as such rather than silently skipped. WHICH repository gets observed is also decided by tools.json, not by this file -- an independent Security Reviewer showed that letting this lower-trust file choose the observation target let a single edited URL here report an affirmative NO_DRIFT forever; a disagreement between the two files is now surfaced, never silently resolved. Two fields below are DECLARATIVE INTENT ONLY and are not read by the checker: each entry's `watch` array (the same global rule set applies to every entry) and `cadence` (the real cadence is the workflow cron). `reviewedRefSource` is likewise not read -- the trusted catalog path is hard-coded, so it cannot be repointed at another file.

notWatchedYet.$comment: Design Section 15.2 also names Superpowers and the OpenWiki provider integration as intended watch targets. Both are recorded in tools.json with `source: "detected-locally"` and no reviewed upstream ref, so there is no exact upstream source to observe and no baseline to compare against -- watching them would mean inventing a source KRYLO never actually reviewed. They are listed here explicitly so the gap is visible rather than silently absent, and become watchable the moment their tools.json record names a real source and reviewed ref.
